recipes.name: Baked Asian-Style Honey Chicken
ingredients_raw: 1 (3 pound) whole chicken, cut into pieces

steps.text: Arrange chicken pieces in a 9x13-inch baking dish. Combine onion, soy sauce, honey, ginger, and garlic in a small bowl; spoon mixture over chicken. Cover the dish and refrigerate to marinate for 1 hour, turning chicken once.
Preheat the oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).

Bake chicken with marinade in the preheated oven for 30 minutes. Turn chicken over and top with green onions, then continue baking until chicken is no longer pink in the center and the juices run clear, 10 to 15 minutes. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center should read at least 165 degrees F (74 degrees C).

raw_recipe.headline: Baked Asian-Style Honey Chicken
raw_recipe.description: This Asian-style honey chicken features a sweet and savory aromatic marinade of soy sauce, ginger, garlic, and onion for a quick, easy baked dinner.

review.reviewBody: The first time I made this I pretty much followed the recipe directions and ingredients. The second time, I got a little more creative and we ended up liking it even more. In addition to the ingredients written, I added 3 Tbls. of vinegar and 1 Tbls. of dijon mustard, which I blended in my food processor. After marinating the chicken, I broiled each chicken piece ten minutes on each side. I then placed the meat in the oven and continued to baste with the sauce. The broiling gave the chicken a nice crispy top and the vinegar and mustard additions added a nice flavor. Great recipe Holly!

Great starting recipe. I recommend you feel free to add more/other flavors you enjoy. As others have noted, I at least double the sauce. I try to cook light, so I use low sodium soy sauce and boneless skinless chicken breasts. I also add a tablespoon of spicy mustard and crushed red pepper for heat. After making the recipe a couple times, I decided on cooking the breasts in the oven on a sheet pan instead of casserole dish. I throw the extra marinade in a sauce pan to reduce and drizzle over the chicken when its done. I have also used this as a stir fry marinade/sauce on the stove top and it works great. I use the leftovers in a salad with ginger dressing... so great!

Came out really good! Didn't change any of the ingredients. I just used 4 bone-in chicken thighs. The measurements remained the same, so I didn't have to double the sauce. I covered them in my casserole dish at 400 for 35 minutes. Then raised it to 425 for 10 minutes. When time was up, I removed the chicken. And in the same casserole dish, I added about 1 tsp of corn starch to thicken the sauce. Then I put the thighs back in the dish and turned to cover. I served it with Lo Mein. Delicious!

I added an extra helping of the sauce, crushed red peppers seasoning, and I drizzled extra honey to the chicken a couple of times. I also broiled the chicken after it was cooked to brown it. Excellent recipe. My fiancé loved it! My new signature dish!

Let me start off by saying this was great! 4 stars instead of 5 is because of the cooking times?? Lowered it to 350 still burnt by skin, but the flavor... yuum. My fiance said quote on quote, this is soo good, the meat is so tender its falling off the bone! I used bone in thighs.. will use legs next time or drumettes, would taste better. I tripled the marinade, put in ziplock bags next time when I have time, will mariande over-night. Used the last batch of marinade to baste while in the oven to keep it moist as it baked. This had a rich asain flavor with a kick. I did add ground red pepper and some red pepper flakes. (everything we eat involves spice) Deffinatly recommend, just think the cooking time is too high. Maybe bake covered?? Can you do that anyone?? Will it cook right/thru?

I've made this a couple of time with a few changes to accomodate what I had on hand, and it was delicious every time. Used garlic scapes that I finely chopped in the Magic Bullet instead of garlic cloves; used 1/4tsp of dried ginger instead of fresh (could probably use a bit more next time); used chicken thighs (skin removed) instead of a whole chicken; used half an onion in the marinade; and omitted the green onions. I use a 9x13 dish as I assume it was a typo in the instructions. I also marinate this overnight as other reviewers have suggested (I can't imagine it would be ready after only an hour of marinating unless you maybe poke holes in the chicken first but then you risk it drying out while baking). I will definitely keep making this recipe!

I put the chicken in a ziplock and let marinade all day and baked in the evening. I put the chicken on a cookie sheet lined with a non-stick tin foil and also sprayed with Pam. I did broil the chicken for 15 minutes and the baked for 45 minutes. Yum!

Quick and easy to prepare. I did make some changes though. I omitted the onion and ginger from the marinade as I had some leftover pineapple, ginger and lemon grass salsa from another recipe on here (it's a scallop recipe) and used that instead. I also added vinegar and grainy Dijon mustard as the top review suggested. Pulsed it all in the food processor then threw everything together and marinated for an hour as written. I recommend cooking the chicken skin side up for the first 30 minutes on your top shelf in the oven to get it crisp. I omitted the green onions as I thought they would burn. Only complaint is that these weren't saucy, so do double the marinade if you want to have some sauce to baste/drizzle over rice (obviously cooked since it's been with raw chicken).

I used the exact amount of sauce in the recipe for 3 bone in chicken thighs and broiled them for 7 minutes about 12 inches from the broiler. After I broiled them, I turned them skin side down and poured the remaining marinade from the bag over them. Baked at 375 for 25 minutes and then flipped them over and baked for another 15 minutes!!! Delicious...even the pickiest kid in the world liked it!!!

This is sooooo yummy! I tripled (at least) the sauce for marinade, and used ziplock bags to marinate overnight. I have baked and also grilled it on the gas grill in disposable baking pans - Each way was super good! I've passed this recipe on to others and they love it too!

I used 4 skinless and bone-in chicken. I covered with aluminum foil and baked in 400 F for the first 20 minutes and reduced the heat to 375 F for the next 30 minutes. I basted every 20 minutes. I removed the cover for the last 10 minutes. Very delicious. I will definitely make this again.

Delicious but a few changes. I was not able to marinate for an hour and I did not have ginger root or green onions. I used 4 TBS of chopped red onion and ground ginger. Sauce was tasty and it all turned out just fine!

Double the proportions and you’re good to go! So flavorful! And I didn’t even marinate for more than 10 minutes. I also seasoned the chicken with salt, pepper, garlic seasoning, and ginger seasoning before pouring the mixture over it though. I also used low sodium soy sauce. Hope you enjoyed like I did!

I think if it didn’t turn out perfect maybe oven temp is off. I did it exactly like it says. It was moist and the aroma filled the house drawing everyone out of their rooms and to the dinner table. Phenomenal. Thank you.

Followed recipe as written with disappointing results. Used all legs and thighs, bone in, with skin trimmed. Marinated 3 hours in zip lock bag. Baked skin side down 30 minutes at 425 in flat metal pan with 3 legs and 3 thighs per pan. After 30 minutes I went to turn the meat but the pan filled up with fat and basically boiled the chicken almost off the bone. Drained and separated fat from juice and basted but the meat never looked anything like the pictures and never got crispy or had a nice coating.
My family loved it - everyone did and that is hard to do in my household! :)
Easy, delicious, family of 7 completely satisfied. I stabbed the chicken with a knife before marinating. Marinated for 2 hours.
Seriously, the best chicken I have had in a long time. I made it with fried rice and baked sweet potatoes. I will definitely be making this again!

Seldom do I just follow a recipe without making changes. But this looked just right, maybe I uped the ginger a bit but only cuz I misjudged and cut a bit more than I should have. We were a bit rushed so it was left for only an hour to infuse the chicken. 12 hours or overnight would certainly boost the flavour profile and really kick it up so many notches. Wowza so good.
